What a Nakshatra is

Vedic astrology divides the Moon's path into 27 Nakshatras, or lunar mansions, each spanning 13 degrees and 20 minutes. Your birth Nakshatra is the one the Moon was in when you were born, and each Nakshatra is further split into four padas, or quarters.

The Nakshatra is one of the most used details in a Vedic chart. It sets the starting point of the Vimshottari dasha sequence, it is one of the factors compared in kundli matching, and its pada is traditionally used to choose the first syllable of a name.

How accurate the result is

Like the Rashi calculator, this uses a simplified formula for the Moon's position. The Moon spends only about a day in each Nakshatra and a few hours in each pada, so a birth time near a boundary can shift the result. For anything important, such as a naming ceremony or kundli matching, have an astrologer confirm it.

Frequently asked

Common questions

How many Nakshatras are there?

There are 27, from Ashwini to Revati, each divided into four padas, which gives 108 padas in all.

What is a pada?

A pada is one quarter of a Nakshatra, about 3 degrees and 20 minutes of the Moon's path. It narrows your birth star down further and is used for naming.

Do I need my exact birth time?

It helps a great deal. The Moon moves through a Nakshatra in about a day, so a time that is out by a few hours can give a different pada or even a different Nakshatra.
